description.ncbi_summary: Lactate dehydrogenase C catalyzes the conversion of L-lactate and NAD to pyruvate and NADH in the final step of anaerobic glycolysis.  LDHC is testis-specific and belongs to the lactate dehydrogenase family.  Two transcript variants have been detected which differ in the 5' untranslated region. [provided by RefSeq, Jul 2008].

uniprot_function.text: Interconverts simultaneously and stereospecifically pyruvate and L-lactate with concomitant interconversion of NADH and NAD(+) (PubMed:35646544). Predominant lactate dehydrogenase isozyme in spermatozoa and spermatogenic cells, where it is required for glycolytic ATP production, sperm motility, capacitation and fertilization (By similarity). Also acts as a regulator of chromatin during late stage of spermatogenesis by acting as a 2-oxoglutarate reductase: translocates into the nucleus and catalyzes the reduction of 2-oxoglutarate to L-2-hydroxyglutarate, thereby regulating centromere condensation and heterochromatin organization (By similarity).
